steps.body: Times have two ways of being said. **7:50 is also 'ten TO eight'** — ten minutes before the next hour. Early in the hour we count PAST the old hour; late in the hour we usually count TO the new one. Same moment, two names.

widget.prompt: Connect each clock time to its spoken name.

pairErrors.feedback: Quarter PAST 7 is 7:15 — fifteen minutes after seven. 7:45 counts the other way: fifteen minutes TO eight.

widget.missFeedback: PAST counts forward from the old hour; TO counts backward from the next one. A quarter is 15 minutes.
widget.successFeedback: 7:15 = quarter past, 7:30 = half past, 7:45 = quarter to 8 — the hour's three landmarks.

predict.prompt: 'Quarter past' the hour means how many minutes past?
predict.reveal: A quarter of the 60-minute hour is 15 — the phrase divides the clock, not the numerals. 'Quarter past' parks the minute hand on the 3.

explanationVariants: 5:50 sits ten minutes before 6:00 — 'ten to six.'
Count the gap to the next hour: 60 − 50 = 10, so ten TO six.

options.label: Ten to six
options.feedback: Ten minutes shy of 6:00 — counting down to the next hour.

options.label: Ten past five
options.feedback: Ten PAST five is 5:10, just after the hour began. 5:50 is deep in the hour — ten minutes TO six.

options.label: Half past five
options.feedback: Half past is 5:30, twenty minutes ago on this clock. 5:50 is nearly at six: ten to.

options.label: Six ten
options.feedback: 6:10 is twenty minutes in the FUTURE — past six o'clock. 5:50 hasn't reached six yet: ten to six.

steps.body: The switch has a formula: **minutes-to = 60 − minutes-past.** At 5:50, that's 60 − 50 = 10 to six. The minute hand shows it too — once it crosses the 6-mark into the clock's left half, counting down to the next hour is the shorter story.

explanationVariants: Hop it: 8:40 → 8:50 → 9:00 is two ten-minute hops.

widget.prompt: The clock reads 8:40. How many minutes TO nine o'clock?

commonErrors.feedback: 40 counts the minutes PAST eight — the question runs the other way. The gap to 9:00 is 60 − 40.
30 would be right at 8:30 — but this clock reads 8:40, ten minutes later, so ten fewer remain: 20.

widget.prompt: Order these times from EARLIEST to latest — translate the names first.

misorderFeedback.feedback: 'Ten to 5' translates to 4:50 — twenty minutes LATER than half past (4:30).
Half past (4:30) comes after quarter past (4:15) — the half is the deeper landmark.

widget.missFeedback: Translate each to clock time: 4:00, 4:15, 4:30, 4:50 — then the order reads itself.
widget.successFeedback: 4:00 → quarter past (4:15) → half past (4:30) → ten to 5 (4:50): one hour, told four ways.

explanationVariants: Quarter TO 3 means 15 minutes before 3:00 — and 3:00 minus 15 is 2:45. Lila nailed it.
Formula check: minutes-past = 60 − 15 = 45, so the clock reads 2:45.

widget.prompt: Lila says 'quarter to 3' means 2:45, 'because a quarter-hour is 15 minutes.' Is she right?

options.label: Yes — quarter TO means 15 minutes before 3:00, which is 2:45
options.feedback: Exactly her thinking: a quarter-hour back from 3:00 lands on 2:45.

options.label: Close — it's 3:15
options.feedback: 3:15 is quarter PAST three. The word TO points backward: fifteen minutes before 3:00 is 2:45.

options.label: It's 2:15
options.feedback: 2:15 is quarter past TWO — a half-hour too early. Counting back 15 from 3:00 lands at 2:45.

options.label: A quarter is 25 minutes, so 2:35
options.feedback: A quarter of the 60-minute hour is 60 ÷ 4 = 15 minutes — the coin is a different quarter!

hints: Translate the bus time first: 'twenty to four' = ?
Marco stands at 3:30 — how far ahead of 3:40 is that?
explanationVariants: 'Twenty to four' is 3:40. Marco arrives at 3:30 — ten minutes ahead of the bus.
Both on one line: 3:30 (Marco) → 3:40 (bus) is a single ten-minute hop.

widget.prompt: The bus leaves at 'twenty to four.' Marco arrives at the stop at 3:30. How many minutes early is he?

commonErrors.feedback: 20 grabbed the number from 'twenty to four' — but that phrase names the BUS time (3:40). Marco's gap is 3:40 − 3:30.
30 read Marco's ':30' as the answer. Translate the bus time (3:40) first, then measure the gap between them.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Step one: twenty-to-four in clock time. Step two: the gap from 3:30 to it.

takeaways: PAST counts forward from the old hour; TO counts back from the next.
A quarter-hour is 15 minutes; the landmarks are :15, :30, :45.

concept.body: Quick rewind. Two direction words: **PAST looks back at the hour you left; TO looks ahead at the hour you're approaching.** 'Ten past 6' = 6:10, just after six. 'Ten to 6' = 5:50, almost six.

explanationVariants: PAST counts forward from six: ten past 6 is 6:10.
The hour named comes FIRST when the word is past — you already reached 6.

options.feedback: 5:50 is ten TO six — approaching it. Ten PAST six means six already happened: 6:10.
6:50 would be ten to SEVEN. Ten past six is just ten minutes in: 6:10.
